hero.headline: Major companies directed tariff refund money to executive bonuses, ProPublica investigation finds
hero.body:
At least nine major companies receiving refunds after the Supreme Court struck down Trump-era tariffs directed portions of that money toward executive bonuses instead of consumer price relief, according to a ProPublica investigation published Monday. The investigation analyzed securities filings and earnings calls to identify companies that told consumers they had to raise prices because of tariffs but are now using refund money for leadership compensation.

Stanley Black & Decker, which makes vacuums, electric drills, and measuring tapes, is expected to receive at least $298 million in tariff reimbursements and indicated some will go to bonuses. The company told consumers it was forced to raise prices because of Trump's import fees. In financial disclosures, Stanley Black & Decker said the refund it received was partially offset by costs for variable incentive compensation, according to ProPublica.

TJX, the parent company of TJ Maxx and Marshalls, received $331 million in refunds and will accrue $112 million in year-end incentive compensation and discretionary bonuses for eligible associates globally because of the refunds, a company spokesperson confirmed to ProPublica. The spokesperson said the company has not disclosed details beyond that accrual because the fiscal year has not ended.

The Trump administration has refunded at least $100 billion to companies since August, about 60 percent of roughly $131 billion in tariffs collected, after the Supreme Court ruled that Trump's tariffs were illegal because they overstepped executive authority and should have required congressional approval. The administration has not specified which companies are receiving refunds despite requests for information. ProPublica found that almost all companies publicly planning to use reimbursements for customer refunds deal with other businesses rather than consumers directly, while some companies have remained vague about their plans for the money.

cards.headline: Software bug disrupts Chase banking nationwide, slowing Zelle and transactions at other banks
cards.body:
A software bug in JPMorgan Chase's on-premise hardware systems disrupted banking services nationwide on Monday, affecting both online access and in-branch transactions and causing delays at other financial institutions. The bank said the issue was not cyber-related and that all customers retained access to their accounts and funds, though servicing some customers was taking longer than usual. Chase said it was working to resolve the problem by the end of the day.

The outage also prevented Chase customers from transferring money via Zelle, the peer-to-peer payment network. A Zelle representative said the technical issues on its platform originated with Chase and that Zelle itself was operating normally. U.S. Bank confirmed its Zelle customers were experiencing issues, though the bank's own systems were not directly impacted. Customers at Wells Fargo also experienced delays, while Capital One said it had not been affected.

Chase said other banks may have been impacted by transaction slowness only to the extent they were party to a transaction with the company, and the issue was not systemically affecting the entire banking system. Regulators were in touch with the affected banks immediately and quickly determined the problem was contained and service restoration was underway, according to a person familiar with the situation. Chase serves approximately 94 million customer relationships in the United States through 5,000 physical branches and 15,000 ATMs.

The Chase outage was the latest in a series of nationwide technology failures over the past week, though there is no evidence the incidents are connected. Microsoft Outlook went offline for approximately 48 hours last week due to what it called a capacity upgrade, and the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop Friday for several hours over what officials said was a botched facilities upgrade. The pattern has raised questions about the resilience of critical systems used by tens of millions of Americans daily.

cards.headline: Nvidia board dismisses campaign to reinstate ousted CEO Jensen Huang as new US export curbs on AI chips take effect
cards.teaser: Board rejects effort backed by Trump and tech leaders to bring back former CEO who resigned over affairs scandal, as administration tightens chip restrictions.
cards.body:
Nvidia's board has dismissed a campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive after he resigned last week following revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy. President Donald Trump said Monday he "would certainly not mind" seeing Huang reinstated, joining SpaceX's Elon Musk and Epic Games' Tim Sweeney among more than 175,000 supporters of the "Bring Jensen Back" campaign.

The Trump administration on Monday announced new restrictions requiring companies in Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Brazil to obtain US export licenses for advanced AI chips, aiming to prevent illegal diversion to China ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping this week. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is leading Nvidia as the company prepares to report earnings Tuesday.

cards.headline: Nasdaq falls more than 2% for third straight day as Nvidia-led AI selloff drags markets lower
cards.teaser: Technology-heavy index extends losses as AI stocks decline ahead of key corporate events this week.
cards.body:
The Nasdaq fell more than 2% on Monday, marking its third consecutive day of declines as Nvidia and other artificial intelligence stocks sold off. The technology-heavy index led broader market losses, with the Dow and S&P 500 also closing lower.

The selloff occurred as investors awaited Nvidia earnings results and the anticipated Anthropic initial public offering later this week. Oil prices also dropped during the session.

cards.headline: Tech leaders claim Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit was orchestrated plot
cards.teaser: Prominent Silicon Valley figures are questioning the circumstances of the CEO's resignation and demanding reinstatement.
cards.body:
Prominent tech leaders are questioning the circumstances surrounding Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years, with many suggesting his departure was orchestrated. Venture capitalist David Sacks and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have challenged reporting that Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive Huang allegedly had an affair with, was a Chinese spy, noting U.S. agencies have not confirmed the allegation.

More than 185,000 people, including Elon Musk, Travis Kalanick, and multiple tech CEOs, have signed a letter calling for Huang's reinstatement. The letter states signers have not seen evidence substantiating spy allegations and argues that suspicion alone is insufficient grounds for ending his leadership.

cards.headline: Portugal boss responds to criticism from Ronaldo's mum
cards.teaser: Jorge Jesus addressed comments by Dolores Aveiro, who said her son had been "deceived" by the manager.
cards.body:
Portugal manager Jorge Jesus responded to criticism from Cristiano Ronaldo's mother, Dolores Aveiro, who said her son had been "deceived" by Jesus. Ronaldo, 41, retired from international football on November 5 after earning 234 caps and scoring 146 goals for Portugal. His retirement came less than a month after he received a 30-day suspension and £215 fine for walking out of the Portugal camp in September when told he would not start against Denmark.

Aveiro, speaking at a Sporting event Monday, expressed satisfaction with Portugal's 4-1 home loss to Denmark on Saturday. Asked about her comments before Tuesday's Nations League match against Wales, Jesus said, "Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo's mother? She is a lady I greatly respect—she suffered a lot to raise her children."

cards.headline: Robert Pattinson named next James Bond, seventh actor to play 007
cards.body:
Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the next actor to play James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced Monday. The 40-year-old British actor becomes the seventh performer to portray the fictional spy in the official film series and will star in the 26th Bond movie, scheduled for release in 2028.

The film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve and written by Steven Knight, though the title and exact release date have not been announced. Pattinson said in a statement that playing Bond is "the honour of a lifetime" and called the role "a dream come true." He added that he is "deeply grateful" to the creative team for their belief in him.

The announcement ends years of speculation about who would succeed Daniel Craig, who appeared in five Bond films over 16 years before his final turn in 2021's No Time to Die. The 2028 release will mark a seven-year gap since the last Bond film, the longest in the franchise's history. Villeneuve, known for the Dune trilogy and films including Arrival and Blade Runner 2049, said Pattinson "has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new."

Pattinson rose to fame in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and starred in the Twilight series, which collectively earned more than $3 billion worldwide. He has since appeared in major films including The Batman and Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, as well as smaller independent productions. He recently worked with Villeneuve on Dune: Part 3, set for release next month.

The film represents a new era for the franchise. Amazon purchased MGM for $8.5 billion in 2021, and in 2025, longtime Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson sold creative control of the series to Amazon MGM, ending the Broccoli family's stewardship that began in 1962.

hero.headline: Houthi rebels seize control of key Red Sea strait as Yemeni army withdraws to defend Aden
hero.body:
Iran-backed Houthi rebels have taken full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and nearby offshore islands after forcing the army of Yemen's internationally recognized government to withdraw from the Red Sea coast to defend the interim capital, Aden. The strait, which accounts for around 12 percent of global trade with 70 to 150 ships passing through daily, connects the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.

The Houthi advance follows the breakdown of a truce with Saudi Arabia in July and a failed government counter-offensive. The rebels seized the initiative with a rapid push down the Red Sea coast, prompting the Yemeni army to retreat. The advance complicates Saudi Arabia's ability to export oil, particularly after a U.S.-Israel war with Iran in February led Tehran to restrict oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia had shifted to pumping oil overland through its East-West Pipeline to a Red Sea terminal at Yanbu, but that pipeline was hit by Houthi drones in July.

Nicholas Hopton, a former British ambassador to Yemen and Iran, said the decision to prioritize Aden's defense over other areas suggests the war is not going well for the Saudi-backed government. He warned that if Aden, a city of roughly 1.25 million, were to fall to the Houthis, it would precipitate further escalation in the regional crisis and additional fragility in the global economy.

Mohammed al-Basha, founder of the U.S.-based Basha Report, said the Houthis would face significant challenges capturing the heavily fortified city and that any attempt would come at a high human cost. He said the rebels appear to be seeking a negotiated surrender by exploiting divisions among southern factions. Former British defense attaché to Yemen Iain Smailes warned the advance could trigger oil price spikes and enable increased weapons smuggling from Iran and the Horn of Africa, extending Iranian and Houthi influence in East Africa.

cards.headline: Five EU countries plan Rwanda deportation hub by 2027
cards.teaser: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands will open a migrant return center in Rwanda, targeting those staying illegally who cannot be returned to their home countries.
cards.body:
Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands announced plans to open a migrant deportation hub in Rwanda in 2027. The facility will accept migrants staying illegally in those countries who are subject to deportation and cannot be returned to their home nations. Deportees will be able to integrate into Rwandan society or return to their home country.

The five governments said the plan complies with EU and international law, though human rights groups raised concerns. Human Rights Watch cited Rwanda's record of repression and arbitrary detention. The hub is expected to initially host about 100 people as a pilot program, with the first phase limited to single men.

cards.headline: UK and EU negotiators finalize post-Brexit food trade reset requiring British alignment with EU rules
cards.teaser: The agreement could cut border costs and boost the economy by £5 billion annually, but Britain will have input on EU food standards without voting power.
cards.body:
Britain and the European Union are set to sign a post-Brexit food trade agreement on Friday that the British government claims could add £5 billion annually to the economy and reduce household food costs. The reset will eliminate hundreds of pages of export paperwork and veterinary checks that have cost companies millions and caused some to stop EU exports entirely since 2020.

In exchange for restored access to EU markets, Britain will align with EU food safety standards but will have a voice in shaping rules without voting power. EU affairs minister Hamish Falconer acknowledged the arrangement makes Britain a "rule taker" on food policy. The deal includes a potential exit clause allowing future governments to reverse the alignment, addressing EU concerns about dismantled border facilities.

cards.headline: Krakow mass shooting suspect dies in hospital as Polish prosecutors say motive investigation continues
cards.teaser: The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Pol
cards.body:
The gunman suspected of killing six people in central Krakow and three family members at their home died in a hospital early Monday morning, Polish police said. The 24-year-old Pol

The 24-year-old Polish man was shot by police officers within three minutes of opening fire in the city's Main Market Square on Saturday afternoon. He had been hospitalized with injuries sustained during a gunfight with responding officers.

cards.headline: France accuses Iran's Revolutionary Guard of orchestrating cyberattacks on European supermarket refrigeration systems
cards.teaser: France has formally accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyberattacks that sabotaged supermarket refrigeration systems across France and Europe last mo
cards.body:
France has formally accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of orchestrating cyberattacks that sabotaged supermarket refrigeration systems across France and Europe last mo

Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that France had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris and said the government would impose sanctions on those responsible. Iran has not officially responded, though some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.

hero.headline: Massachusetts judge sets March 2027 retrial for woman accused of killing three children after hung jury
hero.body:
A Massachusetts judge set a March 29, 2027, trial date for Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of murdering her three children, after a jury deadlocked in her first trial in September. Judge William Sullivan rejected a defense motion last week to dismiss the case on double jeopardy grounds, clearing the way for the retrial. Prosecutors indicated they intend to seek a jury trial, which the defense interpreted as a signal that Clancy, 36, will again face first-degree murder charges, though the district attorney has not formally announced the charges.

Clancy was charged with three counts of first-degree murder in the deaths of her children, five-year-old Cora, three-year-old Dawson, and eight-month-old Callan, who were strangled at the family home in Duxbury on January 24, 2023. It was not disputed at trial that Clancy strangled the children with exercise bands in the basement shortly after she asked her now ex-husband, Patrick Clancy, to leave the house to pick up takeout food and medicine. The defense argued she should be found not guilty by reason of insanity, contending she had severe postpartum psychosis.

Judge Sullivan declared a mistrial on September 4 after the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict. Some jurors later told media outlets they had been ready to find Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, but one juror held out. Double jeopardy protects defendants from being prosecuted more than once for the same crime after an acquittal or conviction, but the legal principle does not apply when a jury deadlocks without reaching a verdict.

The case has renewed debate over how postpartum mental illness is treated in the United States legal system. Clancy is currently held in a state-run psychiatric hospital and medical facility in Massachusetts. Prosecutors had requested a May trial date, but Judge Sullivan, who is set to retire in June, scheduled the retrial for March instead.

cards.headline: Forensic pathologist disputes Epstein suicide ruling, tells BBC autopsy photos suggest homicide
cards.teaser: Expert says review of medical examiner's file points to strangulation from behind.
cards.body:
Expert says review of medical examiner's file points to strangulation from behind.

A forensic pathologist told BBC Newsnight that his review of autopsy photographs suggests Jeffrey Epstein was strangled in a homicide, contradicting the official 2019 suicide ruling. Professor Michael Freeman, who has served as a cause-of-death expert to state attorneys general, said injuries including a deep shoulder hemorrhage, apparent facial trauma, and fingernail marks above the ligature line are consistent with strangulation from behind.

cards.headline: ICE detains 8-year-old Haitian boy at routine check-in after TPS termination, prompting San Diego school district response
cards.teaser: Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him
cards.body:
Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained an 8-year-old Haitian boy at a routine appointment in downtown San Diego last week, separating him from his uncle and transferring him

The boy, a third grader at Fay Elementary School, lost his Temporary Protected Status protections this summer after a Supreme Court decision allowed President Donald Trump to end TPS for Haitians. He was summoned to meet with ICE officers Wednesday, and his uncle brought him to the appointment to comply with the law, according to a letter San Diego Unified School District officials sent Friday to the Department of Homeland Security and the Department of Health and Human Services.

cards.headline: House GOP report faults Justice Department for decades of failures in Epstein case, urges reinterviewing witnesses
cards.teaser: The House Oversight Committee released a Republican-led report Tuesday criticizing the Justice Department for its handling of the Jeffrey Epstein investigation over multiple decade
cards.body:
The House Oversight Committee released a Republican-led report Tuesday criticizing the Justice Department for its handling of the Jeffrey Epstein investigation over multiple decade

The 137-page report stated that too many survivors and witnesses were never approached or properly questioned by federal authorities and urged the DOJ to interview or reinterview individuals who were part of the inner circle of Epstein and co-conspirator Ghislaine Maxwell. Committee Chair James Comer said Epstein operated with impunity, shielded by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims.

cards.headline: Philadelphia boycott of Jewish-owned restaurants draws dueling protests, three arrests
cards.teaser: A bicycle demonstration organized to promote a boycott of Jewish-owned restaurants drew roughly 300 pro-Palestinian protesters and 200 counter-protesters to Philadelphia on Sunday,
cards.body:
A bicycle demonstration organized to promote a boycott of Jewish-owned restaurants drew roughly 300 pro-Palestinian protesters and 200 counter-protesters to Philadelphia on Sunday,

Philadelphia police arrested a woman on an assault charge, a man on disorderly conduct, and a 17-year-old on an assault on police charge, according to a police spokesperson. Officers formed lines to keep the opposing groups separated as tensions escalated.

cards.headline: Supreme Court allows border wall construction in Texas Big Bend region in 8-1 ruling
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 on Monday to allow the Trump administration to proceed with border wall construction in the Big Bend region of southwest Texas, lifting a lower court in
cards.body:
The Supreme Court ruled 8-1 on Monday to allow the Trump administration to proceed with border wall construction in the Big Bend region of southwest Texas, lifting a lower court in

The court found that the federal judge who blocked construction lacked authority to do so and said the administration was extremely likely to prevail on that issue. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the lone dissenter.

cards.headline: Companies used Trump tariff refunds for executive bonuses, investigation finds
cards.teaser: At least nine major companies directed tariff reimbursement funds toward leadership compensation instead of consumer price relief, ProPublica reports.
cards.body:
At least nine major companies including Stanley Black & Decker and TJX directed tariff refund money toward executive bonuses instead of lowering consumer prices, according to a ProPublica investigation. The findings come after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's tariffs as illegal, prompting the administration to refund at least $100 billion to companies since August.

Stanley Black & Decker, which raised prices citing tariff costs, is expected to receive at least $298 million in reimbursements with some going to bonuses. cards.headline: Qantas to outsource 850 jobs to Accenture, most moving to India
cards.teaser: Qantas will outsource 850 corporate jobs to consulting firm Accenture, with most of the positions moving to India, as the Australian airline accelerates investment in artificial in
cards.body:
Qantas will outsource 850 corporate jobs to consulting firm Accenture, with most of the positions moving to India, as the Australian airline accelerates investment in artificial in

Chief Executive Vanessa Hudson announced the plan in an internal email to staff on Tuesday, saying the job cuts will begin in mid-2027. The outsourcing will start with finance, procurement, human resources, and marketing roles shifting mostly to teams in India and some to Australia.

cards.headline: Anthropic sets $70-78 IPO price range, targeting up to $1.4 trillion valuation in largest-ever tech offering
cards.teaser: Anthropic, the startup behind the Claude AI assistant, on Tuesday set an initial public offering price range of $70 to $78 per share, positioning what could become the largest IPO
cards.body:
Anthropic, the startup behind the Claude AI assistant, on Tuesday set an initial public offering price range of $70 to $78 per share, positioning what could become the largest IPO

At the midpoint, the company would raise $61 billion and achieve a valuation of roughly $1.1 trillion when combined with options and unvested stock. At the top of the range, Anthropic could be valued at $1.4 trillion.

cards.headline: Nvidia hires outside law firm for independent investigation into CEO's relationship with alleged Chinese spy
cards.teaser: Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation into Chief Executive Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman alleged to b
cards.body:
Nvidia has hired New York law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation into Chief Executive Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman alleged to b

The company announced Tuesday that attorney Joon Kim, a former U.S. Attorney for New York's Southern District, will lead the probe.

hero.headline: Wyndham exposed millions of customer records after hardcoded password found in Android app
hero.teaser: Hotel giant Wyndham acknowledged a security incident after a researcher discovered a hardcoded password in its Android app that granted access to an internal database containing pe
hero.body:
Hotel giant Wyndham acknowledged a security incident after a researcher discovered a hardcoded password in its Android app that granted access to an internal database containing personal information for millions of rewards members. Security researcher Robert Wiggins found the credential embedded in the app's source code, which allowed access to a Salesforce-hosted database storing customer names, email addresses, member numbers, and login tokens.

The database contained millions of entries from Wyndham's 129 million enrolled rewards members, though Wiggins could not determine an exact count of exposed records. The credential was revoked after Wiggins contacted Wyndham through a journalist because the company had no public channel for reporting security vulnerabilities. A Wyndham spokesperson said the company addressed the issue and found no evidence of unauthorized access, but declined to say whether server logs existed to verify that claim.

Wyndham would not disclose how long the password was embedded in the app, whether it plans to notify affected customers, or whether it will report the incident to the Securities and Exchange Commission as required for material cybersecurity events at public companies. Hardcoded credentials are considered a critical security weakness because anyone with the software can extract and use the password, and such vulnerabilities typically receive maximum severity ratings.

This marks the second major discovery of hardcoded credentials by Wiggins in two weeks, following a similar flaw in the Applebee's app. Wiggins used artificial intelligence tools to scan decompiled app code for such weaknesses. Wyndham's cybersecurity director provided an email address for researchers to report issues, but the company declined to say whether it would establish a formal vulnerability disclosure program or update its website to publicize the reporting channel.

Wyndham experienced a separate security incident in 2024 when hotel check-in computers were found running remote-access spyware that leaked guest records to the internet. That spyware company was later hacked and shut down, and its owner was convicted of making and selling unlawful spyware.

cards.headline: Infoblox confirms hackers accessed company data through compromised SharePoint vendor
cards.teaser: The cybersecurity giant says unauthorized access occurred through a third-party data migration vendor, with customer data reportedly taken.
cards.body:
Cybersecurity and networking giant Infoblox confirmed hackers accessed company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor. The company said it activated incident response procedures and is working with outside cybersecurity experts to investigate the breach.

Two people with knowledge of the incident told TechCrunch the breach involved a vendor providing SharePoint migration services, and one person said sensitive customer data was taken. Infoblox said no company products, cloud services, or software updates were involved in the breach. The company did not identify the vendor or disclose how many customers were affected.

cards.headline: Apple announces macOS 27.3 security controls to limit AI agent privacy risks
cards.teaser: New settings split device permissions and add transparency warnings as AI agents demand full disk access on Macs.
cards.body:
Apple announced security changes in macOS 27.3 designed to protect users from privacy risks posed by AI agents that operate across files and apps on their computers. The company will split Device Control and Data Access into two settings—System & App Protection Override and Accessibility—and require users to select apps from a list when granting permissions.

The update adds transparency indicators when one app controls another and allows users to configure apps to request permission each time access is needed. Apple will also provide guidance warning users that enabling Full Disk Access puts all data on their Mac at risk. The changes follow incidents involving Meta's Muse app and a ChatGPT Mac app security flaw.

cards.headline: Hyperscale data centers consumed up to 2.2 percent of US electricity in one year, study finds
cards.teaser: New research estimates the facilities used power comparable to an entire state's consumption.
cards.body:
Hyperscale data centers operating in the United States consumed between 68 and 99 terawatt-hours of electricity from May 2024 through April 2025, according to a new study. That represents 1.5 to 2.2 percent of total national electricity use, comparable to consumption by Wisconsin or Indiana.

Researchers identified 403 facilities with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts. The study could not distinguish between artificial intelligence computing and traditional data services. Actual power usage varied based on workload type, with conventional data centers running at roughly 48 percent of capacity while AI training operations ran closer to 70 percent.

cards.headline: US hyperscale data centers consumed 82 terawatt-hours of electricity in past year, more than most countries
cards.teaser: Fossil fuels supplied over half the power, producing carbon emissions comparable to Denmark's annual footprint.
cards.body:
A study published in Nature Sustainability found that 403 hyperscale data centers in the United States consumed about 82 terawatt-hours of electricity between May 2024 and April 2025, representing 1.8 percent of total US electricity consumption. That exceeds the annual electricity use of 148 individual countries, including Austria, Israel, and Venezuela, according to researchers.

The facilities produced 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, comparable to Denmark's annual carbon footprint, because about 54 percent of their electricity came from gas and coal. The study used satellite imagery and Environmental Protection Agency data to estimate power consumption and emissions at the massive structures, many built to support generative artificial intelligence.

cards.headline: Shareholders sue Intel, CEO, and CFO over alleged concealment of PC sales slump impact
cards.teaser: Class-action lawsuit claims Intel misled investors before a 28.6 percent single-day stock drop in October.
cards.body:
Shareholders filed a class-action lawsuit against Intel, Chief Executive Officer Lip-Bu Tan, and Chief Financial Officer David Zinsner on Friday in federal court in San Jose, California. The complaint alleges Intel made false and misleading statements between July 23 and October 29 by failing to disclose the full impact of a PC market sales slump on its third-quarter results and beyond. Intel stock dropped 28.6 percent on October 30.

The plaintiffs claim Intel concealed how rising PC component prices affected sales for its partners, substrate supply constraints limiting data center CPU production, and that gains from artificial intelligence-related data center construction were more than offset by declining PC sales. The lawsuit seeks unspecified damages for shareholders during the stated period.

cards.headline: AT&T sues Comcast over 'fiber-powered' internet marketing
cards.teaser: Lawsuit claims Comcast's Xfinity ads mislead consumers because most connections use coaxial cable for the last mile, not fiber to the home.
cards.body:
AT&T filed a lawsuit Friday accusing Comcast of false advertising for marketing its Xfinity internet service as "fiber-powered." The lawsuit argues that while Comcast has deployed fiber throughout its network, the final connection to most homes uses copper coaxial cable rather than fiber optics, resulting in asymmetrical speeds unlike true fiber-to-the-home service.

AT&T claims the fiber-powered description misleads consumers into believing Xfinity is comparable to fiber-to-the-home offerings. Comcast has deployed fiber to the home in only small portions of its territory while advertising the fiber-powered claim broadly. AT&T previously faced criticism for advertising its 4G LTE service as "5G Evolution," which regulators found likely misled consumers.

hero.headline: Former delivery driver Joe Dean earns PGA Tour card after remarkable rise
hero.body:
Former supermarket delivery driver Joe Dean earned a place on the PGA Tour after finishing the season-ending World Tour Championship on Sunday, capping a whirlwind year for the English golfer. Dean, 32, was ranked 2,930th in the world two years ago while working part time to fund his golf career. He secured the 10th and final qualifying spot in the Race to Dubai rankings after a last-hole bogey by Mikael Lindberg moved him back into position, having briefly dropped out after shooting two over par in his final round.

Dean's breakthrough came in August when he won the British Masters, his first DP World Tour victory in his 70th event. That win earned him £440,000 in prize money, more than he had made in total from his previous 19 tournaments in the 2026 season. In July, he had earned a place at The Open after winning the inaugural Last-Chance Qualifier. His PGA Tour card will allow him to compete for more lucrative prize money on the American circuit.

Despite his impressive rise, Dean recently told Today's Golfer that he finds the sport stressful. He said that if he could earn a better living doing something else, he probably would, adding that even when playing well, he does not find it fun due to the pressure. He said he finds relaxing activities like sitting by a fishing lake or cleaning his car more enjoyable.

Patrick Reed also secured his return to the PGA Tour after a four-year absence. The 36-year-old American and 2018 U.S. Masters champion left LIV Golf at the start of this year to play on the DP World Tour, then won two tournaments early in the season to earn one of the 10 PGA Tour cards available through the European circuit.

cards.headline: Andy Robertson becomes Scotland's most-capped men's international
cards.teaser: The captain surpassed Kenny Dalglish's 40-year-old record with his 103rd appearance in a Nations League match against Switzerland.
cards.body:
Andy Robertson became Scotland's most-capped men's international on Monday, starting against Switzerland in a Nations League match to reach 103 appearances. The Tottenham Hotspur left-back surpassed Kenny Dalglish, whose record of 102 caps had stood since 1986.

Robertson, 32, made his Scotland debut in 2014 and has captained the team since 2018. He has led Scotland at three major tournaments and has started 101 of his 103 international appearances. Aston Villa midfielder John McGinn sits eight caps behind Robertson on the all-time list.

cards.headline: Scotland captain Robertson says team 'don't have time' to improve after 4-0 Switzerland defeat
cards.teaser: Andy Robertson rejected calls for patience following a Nations League loss that left Scotland third in their group.
cards.body:
Scotland captain Andy Robertson said the team does not have time to turn things around after a 4-0 defeat by Switzerland left them third in their Nations League group. Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli, appointed in August, has called for patience as he implements a more attacking style, but Robertson dismissed that approach following the loss in St Gallen on Monday.

Robertson, who surpassed Kenny Dalglish as Scotland's most capped men's player, said the team must improve immediately. Pocognoli has won just two of his first six matches in charge, both against North Macedonia, while conceding 10 goals. Scotland will not play again until March.

cards.headline: All Blacks coach Rennie says team 'let the country down' after historic Wales loss
cards.teaser: New Zealand head coach demands a reaction against England following the team's first defeat to Wales in 73 years.
cards.body:
New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie said the All Blacks "let the country down" after their historic 35-28 defeat to Wales in Cardiff, the team's first loss to the Welsh in 73 years. Rennie vowed not to brush the result "under the carpet" ahead of Saturday's match against England at Twickenham.

Rennie praised Wales as "clinical and passionate" but lamented his team's wastefulness in Welsh territory during the final quarter. Several key players including Damian McKenzie, Jordie Barrett, and Codie Taylor will return for the England match as New Zealand looks to avoid consecutive losses in the Nations Championship.

cards.headline: England's Will Joseph set to start against New Zealand after five-try performance
cards.teaser: The wing became only the fifth England men's player to score five tries in one match during Saturday's win over Japan.
cards.body:
England wing Will Joseph is expected to start in Saturday's Nations Championship match against New Zealand after scoring five tries against Japan. The 24-year-old became only the fifth England men's player to score five tries in one match during the 78-15 victory, including a hat-trick in the first 19 minutes.

Joseph also led England with 224 meters carried and a top speed of 21.7 mph. With Immanuel Feyi-Waboso ruled out by an ankle injury, Joseph is in position to retain his wing role for the meeting with the All Blacks at Twickenham.

cards.headline: Cameroon, Senegal and Benin near Afcon 2027 qualification with away wins
cards.teaser: Three nations moved to the brink of qualifying for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations with victories, while Ghana secured consecutive wins over Somalia.
cards.body:
Cameroon, Senegal and Benin each earned away victories to reach 10 points in their respective groups after four rounds of Africa Cup of Nations qualifying. Senegal defeated Sudan 4-2 after surrendering a two-goal lead, Cameroon cruised past Namibia 3-0, and Benin secured a 1-0 win over Central African Republic with a stoppage-time goal. All three teams will qualify for the 2027 finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda if other results favor them Tuesday.

Ghana defeated Somalia 1-0 on Jordan Ayew's first-half penalty to claim back-to-back victories in Group C. The match was played in Ghana because Somalia lacks a stadium suitable for international competition. Ghana moved to six points after losing their opening two matches under former coach Carlos Queiroz.

cards.headline: Portugal boss responds to criticism from Ronaldo's mum
cards.teaser: Jorge Jesus addressed comments by Dolores Aveiro, who said her son had been "deceived" by the manager.
cards.body:
Portugal manager Jorge Jesus responded to criticism from Cristiano Ronaldo's mother, Dolores Aveiro, who said her son had been "deceived" by Jesus. Ronaldo, 41, retired from international football on November 5 after earning 234 caps and scoring 146 goals for Portugal. His retirement came less than a month after he received a 30-day suspension and £215 fine for walking out of the Portugal camp in September when told he would not start against Denmark.

Aveiro, speaking at a Sporting event Monday, expressed satisfaction with Portugal's 4-1 home loss to Denmark on Saturday. Asked about her comments before Tuesday's Nations League match against Wales, Jesus said, "Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo's mother? She is a lady I greatly respect—she suffered a lot to raise her children."

hero.headline: Robert Pattinson named next James Bond, seventh actor to play 007
hero.body:
Robert Pattinson has been confirmed as the next actor to play James Bond, Amazon MGM Studios announced Monday. The 40-year-old British actor becomes the seventh performer to portray the fictional spy in the official film series and will star in the 26th Bond movie, scheduled for release in 2028.

The film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve and written by Steven Knight, though the title and exact release date have not been announced. Pattinson said in a statement that playing Bond is "the honour of a lifetime" and called the role "a dream come true." He added that he is "deeply grateful" to the creative team for their belief in him.

The announcement ends years of speculation about who would succeed Daniel Craig, who appeared in five Bond films over 16 years before his final turn in 2021's No Time to Die. The 2028 release will mark a seven-year gap since the last Bond film, the longest in the franchise's history. Villeneuve, known for the Dune trilogy and films including Arrival and Blade Runner 2049, said Pattinson "has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new."

Pattinson rose to fame in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and starred in the Twilight series, which collectively earned more than $3 billion worldwide. He has since appeared in major films including The Batman and Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, as well as smaller independent productions. He recently worked with Villeneuve on Dune: Part 3, set for release next month.

The film represents a new era for the franchise. Amazon purchased MGM for $8.5 billion in 2021, and in 2025, longtime Bond producers Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson sold creative control of the series to Amazon MGM, ending the Broccoli family's stewardship that began in 1962.

cards.headline: Judge dismisses four claims against Priscilla Presley in business dispute, allows allegations tied to Lisa Marie's death
cards.teaser: A Los Angeles judge tossed four of 21 claims filed by former business advisers but declined to strike references to Lisa Marie Presley's 2023 death from the lawsuit.
cards.body:
A Los Angeles County judge dismissed four claims against Priscilla Presley filed by former business advisers Brigitte Kruse and Kevin Fialko in their $50 million fraud and breach of contract lawsuit. Judge Mark Epstein ruled allegations that Presley interfered with a cosmetics contract and improperly used her own name, image, and likeness were not sufficiently supported. Ten other claims related to fraud, breach of contract, and alleged misappropriation of funds remain.

Presley failed to persuade the judge to remove allegations concerning her daughter Lisa Marie Presley's 2023 death, including claims she prematurely ended life support for financial gain. The judge called portions of the complaint "gratuitous and mean-spirited" but said the disputed language was already public. Lisa Marie died after hospitalization with a small bowel obstruction.

cards.headline: Mavis Staples headlines National Folk Festival in Jackson days after Mississippi's first Black U.S. Senator elected since Reconstruction
cards.teaser: The soul icon, 87, celebrated Scott Colom's historic win while performing at the three-day event, drawing connections to her Civil Rights legacy.
cards.body:
Mavis Staples headlined the National Folk Festival in Jackson, Mississippi, three days after voters elected Scott Colom as the state's first Black U.S. Senator since Reconstruction. The 87-year-old soul icon told a crowd of 2,000 that she was more proud than ever to be from Mississippi, drawing connections between the election and her Civil Rights legacy with the Staple Singers.

Staples received three 2027 Grammy nominations on Monday for her latest album. The three-day festival featured Mississippi artists including Hill Country blues musician Cedric Burnside and gospel quartet Annie and the Caldwells, alongside national and international performers.

cards.headline: DJ John Summit criticizes Grammys dance categories after snub, draws backlash
cards.teaser: The producer called the nominations a "joke" and claimed artists like Madonna and Robyn are "just not dance music."
cards.body:
The producer called the nominations a "joke" and claimed artists like Madonna and Robyn are "just not dance music."

DJ-producer John Summit criticized the Grammy Awards on social media after his second album, Ctrl Escape, received no nominations. Summit wrote that he would not submit work to the Grammys again, calling the dance and electronic music categories a "joke" dominated by "music industry fueled pop stars" rather than "real electronic music & dj's." He singled out nominees including Madonna, Robyn, Tinashe, and Slayyyter, claiming they are "just not dance music" and that "no DJ is playing that music in the clubs." The comments drew sharp criticism online.

cards.headline: Hulu renews 'Reasonable Doubt' for fifth season ahead of Season 4 finale
cards.teaser: The legal drama starring Emayatzy Corinealdi has been streamed for over 150 million hours globally since its 2022 debut.
cards.body:
Hulu and Onyx Collective have renewed the legal drama "Reasonable Doubt" for a fifth season, with the announcement coming just before the Season 4 finale scheduled for November. Season 4 is the show's most-watched season to date, with the series having been streamed for over 150 million hours globally since its 2022 debut.

The renewal will make "Reasonable Doubt" one of Hulu's longest-running scripted shows by season count. The series stars Emayatzy Corinealdi as attorney Jax and is created, written, and executive produced by Raamla Mohamed Hunter, with Kerry Washington among the executive producers.

cards.headline: Variety's 10 Comics to Watch for 2026 perform at New York Comedy Festival showcase
cards.teaser: Rising comedians honored by the magazine each delivered seven-minute sets at a Manhattan venue.
cards.body:
Variety's 10 Comics to Watch for 2026 performed at the New York Comedy Festival on Thursday, delivering stand-up, sketch, and musical acts at the Venue on Music Row at the Hard Rock Hotel in Manhattan. Each comedian performed a seven-minute set before accepting awards.

Performers included Josh Ocean Thomas, Adam Friedland, Eilise Patton, Shapel Lacey, Wally Baram, Usama Siddiquee, and Olivia Carter. Kyle Gordon closed the showcase with a full-band performance of rock parodies. Variety launched the annual franchise in 2000 and has previously honored comedians including Zach Galifianakis, Maria Bamford, Wanda Sykes, Nathan Fielder, and Nikki Glaser.

cards.headline: Donnie Dunagan, voice of Bambi in 1942 Disney classic, dies at 92
cards.teaser: Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.
cards.body:
Donnie Dunagan, the child actor who voiced the title character in Disney's 1942 animated film Bambi, has died of lung cancer, his agents confirmed. Dunagan died Nov. 4. He was 92.

Dunagan's brief acting career spanned just seven films over a few years but included two enduring roles. At age four, he made his film debut in 1938's Mother Carey's Chickens.

hero.headline: Trump nominates OMB official Eric Ueland to head GAO watchdog agency
hero.body:
President Donald Trump has nominated Eric Ueland as comptroller general and head of the Government Accountability Office, a position empowered to sue the administration on behalf of Congress. The nomination represents a push to confirm an ally before Democrats take control of Congress in January. Ueland currently serves as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget, which has led efforts to withhold and cancel federal funding.

The Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee will hold a hearing on the nomination Thursday. Lawmakers in both parties have called for the GAO to challenge the Trump administration before the Supreme Court for withholding federal funds approved by Congress. The agency has issued more than a half-dozen findings of illegal impoundment of federal dollars since the start of Trump's second term but has not yet taken legal action.

Ueland has significant Capitol Hill experience as a former staff director for Senate Budget Committee Republicans under then-Chair Michael Enzi of Wyoming and chief of staff to former Republican Senate Majority Leader Bill Frist. He served as White House director of legislative affairs during the first Trump administration, where he brokered talks between then-Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin and senators on a Covid-19 economic relief package.

Democrats have criticized Republicans for what they call a sham confirmation process that breaks precedent for how the comptroller general is typically nominated. Some Republican senators, particularly those leaving office in January, could question whether it is appropriate to confirm a sitting executive branch official to a position responsible for investigating that same administration. The Supreme Court suggested last fall that the GAO is the only entity with standing to sue the Trump administration for violating the Impoundment Control Act. The agency has been operating under an acting comptroller general since last December.

cards.headline: Congressional Budget Office Director Phillip Swagel to retire in January
cards.teaser: His departure sets up a major appointment decision for incoming Democratic committee leaders.
cards.body:
Phillip Swagel, who has led the Congressional Budget Office since 2019, announced Monday he will retire when his term ends in January. He plans to return to teaching economics at the University of Maryland.

His exit positions Representative Brendan Boyle of Pennsylvania and Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia, the incoming Democratic chairs of the House and Senate Budget committees, to recommend a successor. Congressional leaders then appoint the director based on that recommendation. Swagel previously served as assistant Treasury secretary under President George W. Bush.

cards.headline: Van Hollen declines to rule out challenging Schumer for Senate Democratic leader as caucus debates strategy
cards.teaser: Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode abou
cards.body:
Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland told reporters Monday that he has not ruled out running against Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader, saying he is in listening mode abou

Van Hollen said the party should not have a coronation and that he has not shut the door on a challenge to Schumer, who is currently minority leader and widely expected to be elected to lead the new Senate majority in January. Van Hollen's comments come as some Senate Democrats have withheld support for Schumer while seeking clarity on the party's strategy for the next two years.

cards.headline: Seven Republican senators call for delay in GOP leadership elections
cards.teaser: Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections
cards.body:
Seven Republican senators are calling for the Senate GOP leadership elections to be delayed, with one threatening to skip the vote if the postponement does not occur. The elections

The elections are scheduled for Tuesday, and Senate Majority Leader John Thune of South Dakota is still expected to be reelected to lead the Senate GOP. Senators Ron Johnson of Wisconsin, Rick Scott of Florida, Mike Lee of Utah, Ted Budd of North Carolina, and John Kennedy of Louisiana signed a letter demanding the elections be delayed to allow more discussion about the party's performance last week.

cards.headline: DeSantis positions for 2028 presidential run as Rubio deflects speculation following GOP midterm losses
cards.teaser: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid
cards.body:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis is positioning himself for a 2028 presidential campaign while Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed reports he is considering a White House bid

The maneuvering by both Florida Republicans underscores volatility in the early stages of the 2028 primary, where Vice President Vance had been viewed as a likely frontrunner before Tuesday's election results. DeSantis, whose term as governor ends in January, has fueled speculation through a postelection media campaign that included appearances on podcasts and CNN.

cards.headline: Elon Musk's companies face Democratic investigations after $475 million midterm spending resulted in losses
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4
cards.body:
Elon Musk's business empire faces investigations from congressional Democrats following his emergence as the largest individual donor in the midterm elections, spending at least $4

Armed with subpoena power, Democrats are preparing to examine Musk's Department of Government Efficiency operation, its access to sensitive government data, and whether his companies benefited from his influence over the Trump administration. More than 99 percent of Musk's traceable spending went to losing candidates, according to WIRED.

cards.headline: Jeffries pushes to restrict China chip exports in defense bill
cards.teaser: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C
cards.body:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Monday he will work to include provisions in the annual defense policy bill that would tighten restrictions on advanced chip exports to C

Jeffries told reporters he strongly supports measures currently in the Senate version of the National Defense Authorization Act that would restrict chip access to China and will push to ensure those provisions make it into the final legislation. Jeffries spoke a day after Nvidia's board announced an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
